claims.text: The starting material is a homogeneous solution of multiple noble-metal precursors in near-equiatomic proportions.
Slower, dropwise precursor addition reduces precursor mobility.
Precursor addition kinetics and precursor steady-state times govern the spatial composition and structure of noble-metal HEA nanocrystals.
Inhibiting precursor mobility during low-temperature nanoparticle formation favors formation of a single-phase noble-metal HEA.
Keeping synthesis temperatures below approximately 500 °C prevents excessive precursor mobility and particle growth.
Lower precursor mobility limits local concentration fluctuations.
Lower precursor mobility enhances entropy-driven mixing.
Suppressing early-stage phase segregation produces a more homogeneous, single-phase alloy.
A homogeneous HEA structure fosters charge redistribution and creates isolated noble-metal catalytic sites.
Isolated, electronically modulated noble-metal sites improve catalytic performance by modifying reactant chemisorption.
Dropwise addition at moderate temperature will produce greater nanostructural uniformity than rapid mixing.
The dropwise, moderate-temperature HEA will have a higher catalytic turnover frequency than the rapid-mixing material.
An HEA containing all selected components will be more structurally uniform than a lower-entropy analog missing one noble component.
An HEA containing all selected components will show better catalytic performance than a lower-entropy analog missing one noble component.
The proposed formation and performance relationship should hold generally below approximately 500 °C and in reductive catalytic environments.
The quantitative relationship among dropwise addition rate, nanostructure, and catalytic turnover frequency remains incompletely established.

contradictions.description: The conditions require fixed precursor ratios, while the lower-entropy baseline omits one noble metal and therefore necessarily changes the composition. The phrase 'same overall precursor ratios but with one noble metal omitted' is not internally well-defined.

The intervention proposes systematic control of addition rate and temperature, but the principal falsification comparison changes both simultaneously—dropwise/moderate versus rapid/elevated—so it cannot isolate which intervention caused an observed difference.
